Photogrammetric block survey with a hold on station, sized for a WingtraOne GEN II class aircraft (16 m/s cruise, ~59 min).

The block is flown at 120 m AGL with roughly 200 m line spacing; the 20 km of survey line here covers about 400 ha, which is the coverage this class is sold on. Lines alternate heading by 180 degrees as a real lawnmower pattern does, so in wind half of them are into it.

The hold partway through is the thing a fixed-wing cannot do: stopping to look at something. It is expensive — about 1080 W in still air against about 145 W in cruise — but it gets dramatically cheaper in wind, down to about 210 W at 12 m/s, because holding station means flying at the wind speed through the air and the wing starts carrying the weight. That is translational lift, and it is why hovering into a breeze is easier than in dead calm.
